Translated from the French. The original, Art génératif : de la découverte à la publication d'un projet dans un studio prestigieux, is on my personal site.
One deliberate change in this version: where the French says "art génératif", this one says algorithmic art. The meaning of "generative art" has not changed, but since generative AI took over the word, people who do not know the field tend to assume my projects are made with AI.

You know by now that I am a curious person. I love discovering new disciplines and spending months or years exploring them. I have written before about music production, vegetarianism and the electric guitar.

Here I want to write about the passion that has taken up most of my time these past few years: algorithmic art. From my first scripts producing simple animations, to a show in New York and a drop (a project launch, in our jargon) with one of the most demanding studios in the field, this is the story of an adventure I did not see coming.

Edit: after this piece was published in French, I was invited to give the closing keynote of DevFest Toulouse 2023 on the subject.

Here is a more recent version, presented at MiXiT 2025.

What is algorithmic art?

Algorithmic art is artistic creation, usually digital, that uses algorithms to produce work which generates itself or is not determined in advance.

I will also talk about creative coding, which is a broader definition. It means using programming as a medium of artistic expression in its own right: visual, musical, literary, interactive, performative.

Discovering creative coding, and first steps on Hic Et Nunc

It starts on the day I decide I want to learn to draw. I have no skill at it whatsoever, but I am curious. I like the idea of a new passion disconnected from screens. I picture myself with a notebook and a pencil at a café terrace.

I ask an artist friend to give me a lesson. Her lesson is great, but unsurprisingly I quickly realise I have everything to learn and that the road is long. Before long I want to make more geometric drawings, then to work on an iPad with Procreate to compensate for my lack of dexterity, then to do vector drawing, and then I go back to my computer to code what I had been trying to make. That is how I take my first steps in creative coding.

I start with p5.js, a JavaScript library, probably the most widely used, especially by beginners. You could describe it as Microsoft Paint, but in JavaScript. There are plenty of tutorials, a thorough reference, books, an online editor. I start playing with mathematics, physics, the classic algorithms of the field, noise, randomness.

As I sink further into creative programming, I start following a lot of artists on Instagram and Twitter, learning from their work and experimenting with my own ideas. It is a period of exploration and discovery.

This is when I make my first drops on Hic Et Nunc. I begin by publishing perfect loops, animations that repeat endlessly. To my great surprise those first drops are well received, and I start getting valuable feedback from my very first collectors.

Discovering long-form, and first drops on fx(hash)

From here on I will mostly be talking about long-form, a format popularised by platforms like Art Blocks and fx(hash). The concept works like this:

The artist writes a generative script, which is recorded on a blockchain, making it permanent, immutable and verifiable. The artist then specifies how many iterations, or pieces, can be created from that script, usually a few hundred. When a collector buys an iteration, the script runs to generate a new piece, which is wrapped in an NFT and transferred directly to the collector. When the script runs, nobody knows exactly what will come out of it: not the collector, not the platform, not the artist. It is a surprise for everyone.

I publish, or drop, my first long-form projects on fx(hash) very shortly after it opens. The first one is SEA: a very simple project, made in a few days, from which I learn an enormous amount. 150 animated editions, built quickly just to play with fx(hash).

The pieces find collectors quickly. I talk to some of them and meet nothing but lovely people, as amused as I am at watching what everyone is doing with these platforms, at being spectators to all this ferment and creativity, and generally well informed about algorithmic art and NFTs.

That is how I end up publishing some fifteen projects on the platform in a few months. Each time I try new techniques, question the aesthetics, test new concepts.

Let me tell you about two projects I am particularly attached to.

BRIDGE

BRIDGE is a collaborative project for which I published the code on GitHub and invited any artist who wanted to contribute. It is a long-form project of 520 editions. The concept is simple: write a piece of code that draws a bridge in p5.js, respecting the given positions of the deck slabs. Each minted piece has a default style, but the collector can cycle through all 26 styles on their bridge.

The project introduced me to several artists I still talk to. It is fascinating to see the diversity of styles that came out of identical constraints.

ARTERIA

I also want to mention ARTERIA, probably the fx(hash) project I am proudest of so far. It has 333 editions. At that point I wanted to take more time, to attempt more complex and more considered projects. There is a making-of describing how it works and how it came about in detail.

The name ARTERIA means "artery" in old Occitan. The project is an exploration of autonomous agents: entities that follow a set of simple rules, here in order to draw paths.

In ARTERIA the agents have a default behaviour: they move straight ahead, they reproduce, and they die when they meet the trajectory of another agent. As they move they draw small circles. The system starts from dozens of random initial parameters: level of recursion, position and size of the agents, colours, birth angle, distribution. The possibilities are endless.

Local rules can then be applied on top. All the agents in the upper half might slowly turn, for instance. The final result is the product of the initial parameters, the interactions between agents, and the local rules. It is a piece about the beauty and complexity that can emerge from simple rules and autonomous interaction.

"I would have liked to be an artist"

The ARTERIA drop is a success on fx(hash). I start having collectors who follow my work closely, who buy and share my projects, who advise and support me. It makes me want even more to take my time, to keep working on the aesthetics, to build richer and more complex generators. It is getting serious.

Here is a podcast recorded in June 2022 in which I am interviewed by Lucie-Eleonore Riveron, CEO of the Paris auction house FauveParis. I talk about how I got here, but also about the impostor syndrome that makes it hard for me to think of myself as an artist, about the preconceptions I carry about "real artists", and about what I want to do next.

fx(hash), which I have talked about at length, is an open platform: anyone can post a project whenever they want, and there is a great deal of excellent work on it. But there are many others. Some are equally open; others require the project to be selected by a curation panel. Platforms like gm.studio, or Art Blocks with its Curated section, can be extremely demanding.

So I set myself a challenge: could I too land a drop with one of the platforms I keep admiring from a distance?

FOLRADURA

I keep experimenting with a new long-form project, FOLRADURA, published on 256ART. It explores the creation of organic patterns through a mix of mathematics, physics, noise and chance.

FOLRADURA rests on one main concept: local modifiers. A modifier applies a local effect, an attraction for instance, to a grid of hundreds of thousands of points. What you see is the path of those points, between their initial and their final position. Each edition plays with one or two types of modifier. They can be placed in different ways, sometimes randomly, sometimes on a grid. Each produces very different effects depending on its configuration and on its type: squares, spirals, lines, waves.

Every point is influenced by every modifier. All that complexity produces a very organic look and a great deal of detail. The project was a success, and it showed the aesthetics and complexity that can emerge from simple rules and autonomous interaction. There is a making-of if you want more.

More on FOLRADURA

  • Project page
  • Making-of
  • The project on 256ART

INTRICADA

Having loved working with autonomous agents on ARTERIA, I decided to take the concept back up and push it in a new direction.

The name INTRICADA means "interlaced" in old Occitan. The project explores the balance between emergence and control, a recurring theme in algorithmic art.

INTRICADA is built on autonomous agents similar to those in ARTERIA. The agents draw very small dots and follow simple rules. I designed INTRICADA as a simulation: set initial conditions, then watch what comes out. Each piece is the result of thousands of unforeseeable consequences.

What makes INTRICADA singular is the sheer variety of possible outcomes. Many parameters influence the initial position and direction of the agents, the colour palettes, and much else. Every combination produces a genuinely distinct result.

INTRICADA offers a visual experience on several scales. From a distance a piece can look like intersecting circles, like geometric patterns, like confetti. Closer, you see that those shapes are made of a multitude of agent trajectories. Closer still, you see that those trajectories are made of dots, several hundred thousand per output.

INTRICADA was dropped as an open edition, meaning there was no limit on the number of pieces that could be created, only a time limit. I had the honour of being selected by Bright Moments as their artist of the month in March 2023. What is particular about Bright Moments is their care in giving a physical and human dimension to the projects they publish. INTRICADA was shown in cities around the world: New York, London, Mexico City, Venice Beach, Berlin and Tokyo. An incredible experience.

More on INTRICADA

  • Project page
  • The project on Bright Moments

The Source

Alongside INTRICADA, since July 2022, I had been working on a collaboration with a long-time friend and business partner, Matthieu Segret. From my earliest days in this world I had been telling him about what I was finding. It did not take him long to be tempted himself, and his fx(hash) profile is worth a look.

By the summer of 2022, algorithmic art had been taking up a substantial share of our free time for a year, and we talked about it constantly. An idea slowly took shape: what if we pooled our skills into an artistic collaboration? Find an idea, enjoy ourselves, do our best, and see what came out.

For this project Matthieu wanted to play with textures and try to achieve a physical quality in the render; I wanted to work with mathematical concepts.

That was the start of months of thinking, brainstorming, trials, code, debugging, doubt and joy. After a few months we found our through-line: to represent water abstractly, in its various forms, with coloured reflections drawn from places around the world. During that period we regularly rented places to work together, sometimes by the sea or a river, for the inspiration.

We have already told the story of how the project came together in detail, so let me jump forward a few months.

By early 2023 we were very happy with what we had. It was almost certainly the best project either of us had made. Being two, and spending that much time on it, let us work every detail. We had a project, a name and a presentation deck. Now we had to find somewhere to publish it. We pitched it to several platforms, including the ones I had been dreaming about for a while.

In early May the news came: gm.studio wanted to publish it. What is particular about gm.studio is that the curation panel does not know the artist's name. It makes for a fairer and more inclusive selection, based on the project alone. We love the platform and we love their selection. And to top it off, it was the first time a project had been selected unanimously by the panel. We were more than delighted, and we signed without hesitation.

The Source came out on gm.studio on 31 July 2023. I will let you admire the teaser they made for the occasion.

More on The Source

  • Project page
  • The project on gm.studio
  • The story behind The Source
  • Episode of the NFT Morning podcast (in French)

The Destination, at Bright Moments Paris

The adventure did not stop there. Matthieu and I decided to keep collaborating. Starting from the source code of The Source, we built an entirely new project drawing on the same universe: The Destination.

The Destination is an ode to curiosity, a piece about the diversity of paths one can take and the multitude of subjects there are to discover. Each planet or star represents a field to explore. Matthieu and I combined our own enthusiasms to bring the series to life; it celebrates the whole journey towards a goal as much as reaching it. The title is also a nod to our first collaboration.

The project took us to Bright Moments Paris, where we got to meet collectors of ours, and artists we admire and talk to regularly.

Bright Moments Finale, in Venice

Bright Moments then invited me to work with them again for their final event, this time on a unique project shown during the 2024 Venice Biennale. The piece is singular in that it combines the work of over sixty artists who had been pivotal to the gallery's history.

It was a pleasure to see my work presented in such an extraordinary setting.

Résilience

Résilience is a deeply personal algorithmic project, born of a year exploring visual patterns and textures. It dropped in November 2024 on gm.scribe. Each edition stands for a moment of a life, a trial that was overcome, a slow but real transformation. Drawn from a health experience that had a heavy impact on my life, hyperacusis and tinnitus, the work is about the human capacity to adapt, to heal and to move forward.

Through abstract forms, evolving palettes and a subtle animation, Résilience invites collectors to find, in a given piece, a resonance with their own path. It is a piece about persistence, about rebuilding, and about hope.

It is also my first project on Bitcoin.

What comes next

I have projects in the works, shows and drops on the way. I would also like the chance to show my work, and algorithmic art more broadly, in my own city of Montpellier, or at least in France.

I get a lot of pleasure out of introducing people to this world. I have presented algorithmic art through my own path at DevFest Toulouse in 2023, and more recently at MiXiT and MontpellierJS.

If you want to follow along, it happens on Twitter and Instagram. There is also the GENART podcast.

Thank you to everyone who has been part of this.

blocks.html_en: It starts on the day I decide I want to learn to draw. I have no skill at it whatsoever, but I am curious. I like the idea of a new passion disconnected from screens. I picture myself with a notebook and a pencil at a café terrace.

blocks.html_en: I ask an artist friend to give me a lesson. Her lesson is great, but unsurprisingly I quickly realise I have everything to learn and that the road is long. blocks.html_en: The artist writes a generative script, which is recorded on a blockchain, making it permanent, immutable and verifiable. The artist then specifies how many iterations, or pieces, can be created from that script, usually a few hundred. When a collector buys an iteration, the script runs to generate a new piece, which is wrapped in an NFT and transferred directly to the collector. blocks.html_en: BRIDGE is a collaborative project for which I published the code on GitHub and invited any artist who wanted to contribute. It is a long-form project of 520 editions. blocks.html_en: The name ARTERIA means "artery" in old Occitan. The project is an exploration of autonomous agents: entities that follow a set of simple rules, here in order to draw paths.

sentences.en: The name ARTERIA means "artery" in old Occitan.
sentences.zh: ARTERIA 这个名字在古奥克西唐语中的意思是“动脉”。

blocks.html_en: In ARTERIA the agents have a default behaviour: they move straight ahead, they reproduce, and they die when they meet the trajectory of another agent. As they move they draw small circles. The system starts from dozens of random initial parameters: level of recursion, position and size of the agents, colours, birth angle, distribution. The possibilities are endless.

blocks.html_en: FOLRADURA rests on one main concept: local modifiers. A modifier applies a local effect, an attraction for instance, to a grid of hundreds of thousands of points. What you see is the path of those points, between their initial and their final position. Each edition plays with one or two types of modifier. They can be placed in different ways, sometimes randomly, sometimes on a grid. Each produces very different effects depending on its configuration and on its type: squares, spirals, lines, waves.

blocks.html_en: INTRICADA

sentences.en: INTRICADA
sentences.zh: 简介

blocks.html_en: Having loved working with autonomous agents on ARTERIA, I decided to take the concept back up and push it in a new direction.

sentences.en: Having loved working with autonomous agents on ARTERIA, I decided to take the concept back up and push it in a new direction.
sentences.zh: 由于喜欢在 ARTERIA 上与自主代理合作，我决定重新采用这个概念并将其推向新的方向。

blocks.html_en: The name INTRICADA means "interlaced" in old Occitan. The project explores the balance between emergence and control, a recurring theme in algorithmic art.

sentences.en: The name INTRICADA means "interlaced" in old Occitan.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 这个名称在古奥克西唐语中的意思是“交错”。

sentences.en: The project explores the balance between emergence and control, a recurring theme in algorithmic art.
sentences.zh: 该项目探索了涌现与控制之间的平衡，这是算法艺术中反复出现的主题。

blocks.html_en: INTRICADA is built on autonomous agents similar to those in ARTERIA. The agents draw very small dots and follow simple rules. I designed INTRICADA as a simulation: set initial conditions, then watch what comes out. Each piece is the result of thousands of unforeseeable consequences.

sentences.en: INTRICADA is built on autonomous agents similar to those in ARTERIA.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 建立在与 ARTERIA 类似的自主代理之上。

sentences.en: The agents draw very small dots and follow simple rules.
sentences.zh: 代理绘制非常小的点并遵循简单的规则。

sentences.en: I designed INTRICADA as a simulation: set initial conditions, then watch what comes out.
sentences.zh: 我将 INTRICADA 设计为模拟：设置初始条件，然后观察结果。

sentences.en: Each piece is the result of thousands of unforeseeable consequences.
sentences.zh: 每一件作品都是数以千计的不可预见后果的结果。

blocks.html_en: What makes INTRICADA singular is the sheer variety of possible outcomes. Many parameters influence the initial position and direction of the agents, the colour palettes, and much else. Every combination produces a genuinely distinct result.

sentences.en: What makes INTRICADA singular is the sheer variety of possible outcomes.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 的独特之处在于可能的结果多种多样。

sentences.en: Many parameters influence the initial position and direction of the agents, the colour palettes, and much else.
sentences.zh: 许多参数会影响代理的初始位置和方向、调色板等等。

sentences.en: Every combination produces a genuinely distinct result.
sentences.zh: 每一种组合都会产生真正独特的结果。

blocks.html_en: INTRICADA offers a visual experience on several scales. From a distance a piece can look like intersecting circles, like geometric patterns, like confetti. Closer, you see that those shapes are made of a multitude of agent trajectories. Closer still, you see that those trajectories are made of dots, several hundred thousand per output.

sentences.en: INTRICADA offers a visual experience on several scales.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 提供多种尺度的视觉体验。

sentences.en: From a distance a piece can look like intersecting circles, like geometric patterns, like confetti.
sentences.zh: 从远处看，一件作品看起来就像相交的圆圈、几何图案、五彩纸屑。

sentences.en: Closer, you see that those shapes are made of a multitude of agent trajectories.
sentences.zh: 靠近一点，您会发现这些形状是由大量代理轨迹组成的。

sentences.en: Closer still, you see that those trajectories are made of dots, several hundred thousand per output.
sentences.zh: 再靠近一点，您会发现这些轨迹是由点组成的，每个输出有数十万个点。

blocks.html_en: INTRICADA was dropped as an open edition, meaning there was no limit on the number of pieces that could be created, only a time limit. I had the honour of being selected by Bright Moments as their artist of the month in March 2023. What is particular about Bright Moments is their care in giving a physical and human dimension to the projects they publish. INTRICADA was shown in cities around the world: New York, London, Mexico City, Venice Beach, Berlin and Tokyo. An incredible experience.

sentences.en: INTRICADA was dropped as an open edition, meaning there was no limit on the number of pieces that could be created, only a time limit.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 作为开放版本被放弃，这意味着可以创建的作品数量没有限制，只有时间限制。

sentences.en: I had the honour of being selected by Bright Moments as their artist of the month in March 2023.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸被 Bright Moments 选为 2023 年 3 月的本月艺术家。

sentences.en: What is particular about Bright Moments is their care in giving a physical and human dimension to the projects they publish.
sentences.zh: 《光明时刻》的特别之处在于他们非常注重为他们发布的项目赋予物理和人文维度。

sentences.en: INTRICADA was shown in cities around the world: New York, London, Mexico City, Venice Beach, Berlin and Tokyo.
sentences.zh: INTRICADA 在世界各地的城市展出：纽约、伦敦、墨西哥城、威尼斯海滩、柏林和东京。

sentences.en: An incredible experience.
sentences.zh: 一次难以置信的经历。

blocks.html_en: Alongside INTRICADA, since July 2022, I had been working on a collaboration with a long-time friend and business partner, Matthieu Segret. From my earliest days in this world I had been telling him about what I was finding. It did not take him long to be tempted himself, and his fx(hash) profile is worth a look.

sentences.en: Alongside INTRICADA, since July 2022, I had been working on a collaboration with a long-time friend and business partner, Matthieu Segret.
sentences.zh: 自 2022 年 7 月以来，我一直在与 INTRICADA 一起与我的老朋友兼业务合作伙伴 Matthieu Segret 进行合作。

sentences.en: From my earliest days in this world I had been telling him about what I was finding.
sentences.zh: 从我来到这个世界的最初几天起，我就一直告诉他我的发现。

sentences.en: It did not take him long to be tempted himself, and his fx(hash) profile is worth a look.
sentences.zh: 没过多久他就被诱惑了，他的 fx(hash) 个人资料值得一看。

blocks.html_en: By the summer of 2022, algorithmic art had been taking up a substantial share of our free time for a year, and we talked about it constantly. An idea slowly took shape: what if we pooled our skills into an artistic collaboration? Find an idea, enjoy ourselves, do our best, and see what came out.

sentences.en: By the summer of 2022, algorithmic art had been taking up a substantial share of our free time for a year, and we talked about it constantly.
sentences.zh: 到 2022 年夏天，算法艺术已经占据了我们一年的大部分空闲时间，我们不断地谈论它。

sentences.en: An idea slowly took shape: what if we pooled our skills into an artistic collaboration?
sentences.zh: 一个想法慢慢成形：如果我们将我们的技能集中到艺术合作中会怎样？

sentences.en: Find an idea, enjoy ourselves, do our best, and see what came out.
sentences.zh: 找到一个想法，享受我们自己，尽力而为，看看结果如何。

blocks.html_en: For this project Matthieu wanted to play with textures and try to achieve a physical quality in the render; I wanted to work with mathematical concepts.

sentences.en: For this project Matthieu wanted to play with textures and try to achieve a physical quality in the render; I wanted to work with mathematical concepts.
sentences.zh: 对于这个项目，Matthieu 希望尝试使用纹理并尝试在渲染中实现物理质量；我想研究数学概念。

sentences.en: A brainstorming session with Matthieu
sentences.zh: 与马蒂厄的头脑风暴会议

blocks.html_en: That was the start of months of thinking, brainstorming, trials, code, debugging, doubt and joy. After a few months we found our through-line: to represent water abstractly, in its various forms, with coloured reflections drawn from places around the world. During that period we regularly rented places to work together, sometimes by the sea or a river, for the inspiration.

sentences.en: That was the start of months of thinking, brainstorming, trials, code, debugging, doubt and joy.
sentences.zh: 这是几个月的思考、集思广益、试验、编码、调试、怀疑和喜悦的开始。

sentences.en: After a few months we found our through-line: to represent water abstractly, in its various forms, with coloured reflections drawn from places around the world.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，我们找到了我们的主线：用来自世界各地的彩色倒影以各种形式抽象地代表水。

sentences.en: During that period we regularly rented places to work together, sometimes by the sea or a river, for the inspiration.
sentences.zh: 在那段时期，我们经常租用一些地方一起工作，有时是在海边或河边，以寻找灵感。

blocks.html_en: We have already told the story of how the project came together in detail, so let me jump forward a few months.

sentences.en: We have already told the story of how the project came together in detail, so let me jump forward a few months.
sentences.zh: 我们已经详细讲述了该项目是如何组合在一起的，所以让我先跳到几个月。

blocks.html_en: By early 2023 we were very happy with what we had. It was almost certainly the best project either of us had made. Being two, and spending that much time on it, let us work every detail. We had a project, a name and a presentation deck. Now we had to find somewhere to publish it. We pitched it to several platforms, including the ones I had been dreaming about for a while.

sentences.en: By early 2023 we were very happy with what we had.
sentences.zh: 到 2023 年初，我们对所拥有的一切感到非常满意。

sentences.en: It was almost certainly the best project either of us had made.
sentences.zh: 这几乎肯定是我们做过的最好的项目。

sentences.en: Being two, and spending that much time on it, let us work every detail.
sentences.zh: 作为两个人，花那么多时间在这件事上，让我们处理每一个细节。

sentences.en: We had a project, a name and a presentation deck.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个项目、一个名称和一个演示文稿。

sentences.en: Now we had to find somewhere to publish it.
sentences.zh: 现在我们必须找到一个地方来发布它。

sentences.en: We pitched it to several platforms, including the ones I had been dreaming about for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们将其推广到多个平台，包括我一直梦想的平台。

blocks.html_en: In early May the news came: gm.studio wanted to publish it. What is particular about gm.studio is that the curation panel does not know the artist's name. It makes for a fairer and more inclusive selection, based on the project alone. We love the platform and we love their selection. And to top it off, it was the first time a project had been selected unanimously by the panel. We were more than delighted, and we signed without hesitation.

sentences.en: In early May the news came: gm.studio wanted to publish it.
sentences.zh: 五月初传来消息：gm.studio想要发布它。

sentences.en: What is particular about gm.studio is that the curation panel does not know the artist's name.
sentences.zh: gm.studio 的特别之处在于策展小组不知道艺术家的名字。

sentences.en: It makes for a fairer and more inclusive selection, based on the project alone.
sentences.zh: 仅基于项目，它就可以提供更公平、更具包容性的选择。

sentences.en: We love the platform and we love their selection.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢这个平台，也喜欢他们的选择。

sentences.en: And to top it off, it was the first time a project had been selected unanimously by the panel.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这是第一次由评审团一致选择一个项目。

sentences.en: We were more than delighted, and we signed without hesitation.
sentences.zh: 我们非常高兴，毫不犹豫地签了字。

sentences.en: The Destination, at Bright Moments Paris
sentences.zh: 巴黎光明时刻的目的地

blocks.html_en: The adventure did not stop there. Matthieu and I decided to keep collaborating. Starting from the source code of The Source, we built an entirely new project drawing on the same universe: The Destination.

sentences.en: The adventure did not stop there.
sentences.zh: 冒险并没有就此停止。

sentences.en: Matthieu and I decided to keep collaborating.
sentences.zh: 马蒂厄和我决定继续合作。

sentences.en: Starting from the source code of The Source, we built an entirely new project drawing on the same universe: The Destination.
sentences.zh: 从 The Source 的源代码开始，我们构建了一个基于同一个宇宙的全新项目：The Destination。

blocks.html_en: The Destination is an ode to curiosity, a piece about the diversity of paths one can take and the multitude of subjects there are to discover. Each planet or star represents a field to explore. Matthieu and I combined our own enthusiasms to bring the series to life; it celebrates the whole journey towards a goal as much as reaching it. The title is also a nod to our first collaboration.

sentences.en: The Destination is an ode to curiosity, a piece about the diversity of paths one can take and the multitude of subjects there are to discover.
sentences.zh: 《目的地》是一首对好奇心的颂歌，讲述了人们可以采取的路径的多样性以及有待发现的众多主题。

sentences.en: Each planet or star represents a field to explore.
sentences.zh: 每颗行星或恒星都代表一个值得探索的领域。

sentences.en: Matthieu and I combined our own enthusiasms to bring the series to life; it celebrates the whole journey towards a goal as much as reaching it.
sentences.zh: 马蒂厄和我结合了我们自己的热情，将这个系列变成了现实。它庆祝实现目标的整个旅程。

sentences.en: The title is also a nod to our first collaboration.
sentences.zh: 这个标题也是对我们第一次合作的致敬。

blocks.html_en: The project took us to Bright Moments Paris, where we got to meet collectors of ours, and artists we admire and talk to regularly.

sentences.en: The project took us to Bright Moments Paris, where we got to meet collectors of ours, and artists we admire and talk to regularly.
sentences.zh: 这个项目把我们带到了巴黎的光明时刻，在那里我们见到了我们的收藏家，以及我们欣赏并定期交谈的艺术家。

blocks.html_en: Résilience

sentences.en: Résilience
sentences.zh: 弹力

blocks.html_en: Résilience is a deeply personal algorithmic project, born of a year exploring visual patterns and textures. It dropped in November 2024 on gm.scribe. Each edition stands for a moment of a life, a trial that was overcome, a slow but real transformation. Drawn from a health experience that had a heavy impact on my life, hyperacusis and tinnitus, the work is about the human capacity to adapt, to heal and to move forward.

sentences.en: Résilience is a deeply personal algorithmic project, born of a year exploring visual patterns and textures.
sentences.zh: Résilience 是一个非常个人化的算法项目，诞生于一年来对视觉模式和纹理的探索。

sentences.en: It dropped in November 2024 on gm.scribe.
sentences.zh: 它于 2024 年 11 月在 gm.scribe 上发布。

sentences.en: Each edition stands for a moment of a life, a trial that was overcome, a slow but real transformation.
sentences.zh: 每个版本都代表着生命中的一个时刻，一次被克服的考验，一次缓慢但真实的转变。

sentences.en: Drawn from a health experience that had a heavy impact on my life, hyperacusis and tinnitus, the work is about the human capacity to adapt, to heal and to move forward.
sentences.zh: 这部作品取材于对我的生活产生重大影响的健康经历——听觉过敏和耳鸣，它是关于人类适应、治愈和前进的能力。

blocks.html_en: Through abstract forms, evolving palettes and a subtle animation, Résilience invites collectors to find, in a given piece, a resonance with their own path. It is a piece about persistence, about rebuilding, and about hope.

content_html_zh:
从法语翻译而来。 原创《生成艺术：在著名工作室中从发现到发布一个项目》位于我的个人网站上。 这个版本有一个有意的改变：法语中说“art génératif”，这个版本说的是算法艺术。 “生成艺术”的含义没有改变，但自从生成人工智能接管这个词以来，不了解该领域的人往往会认为我的项目是用人工智能制作的。

你现在知道我是一个好奇的人。 我喜欢发现新学科并花数月或数年的时间探索它们。 我之前写过关于音乐制作、素食主义和电吉他的文章。

在这里，我想写一下过去几年占据我大部分时间的热情：算法艺术。 从我的第一个脚本制作简单的动画，到在纽约的一场演出，以及与该领域要求最高的工作室之一的合作（用我们的行话来说是项目启动），这是一个我没有预见到的冒险故事。

编辑：这篇文章以法语发表后，我受邀就该主题在 2023 年图卢兹 DevFest 上发表闭幕主题演讲。

这是 MiXiT 2025 上发布的更新版本。

什么是算法艺术？

算法艺术是艺术创作，通常是数字化的，它使用算法来产生自行生成或未预先确定的作品。

我还将讨论创意编码，这是一个更广泛的定义。 它意味着使用编程作为艺术表达的媒介：视觉、音乐、文学、互动、表演。

探索创意编码，以及 Hic Et Nunc 上的第一步

从我决定要学画画的那一天开始。 我对此一无所知，但我很好奇。 我喜欢脱离屏幕的新激情的想法。 我想象自己拿着笔记本和一支铅笔在咖啡馆的露台上。

我请一位艺术家朋友给我上一课。 她的教训很棒，但毫不奇怪，我很快意识到我有一切要学习，而且路还很长。 不久之后，我想制作更多的几何图画，然后用 Procreate 在 iPad 上工作，以弥补我灵活性的不足，然后进行矢量绘图，然后我回到电脑前编写我一直在尝试制作的代码。 这就是我迈出创意编码第一步的方式。

我从 p5.js 开始，它是一个 JavaScript 库，可能是使用最广泛的，尤其是初学者。 您可以将其描述为 Microsoft Paint，但是使用 JavaScript。 有大量的教程、详尽的参考资料、书籍和在线编辑器。 我开始研究数学、物理、该领域的经典算法、噪声、随机性。

随着我进一步深入创意编程，我开始在 Instagram 和 Twitter 上关注许多艺术家，从他们的作品中学习并尝试自己的想法。 这是一个探索和发现的时期。

这是我第一次接触 Hic Et Nunc。 我首先发布完美的循环，即无限重复的动画。 令我惊讶的是，第一批产品受到了好评，我开始从我的第一批收藏家那里得到宝贵的反馈。

发现长格式，并首先关注 fx(hash)

从这里开始，我将主要讨论长格式，这是一种由 Art Blocks 和 fx(hash) 等平台流行的格式。 这个概念的运作方式如下：

艺术家编写生成脚本，记录在区块链上，使其永久、不可变且可验证。 然后，艺术家指定可以根据该脚本创建多少次迭代或作品，通常是几百个。 当收藏家购买迭代时，脚本会运行以生成新的作品，该新作品被包装在 NFT 中并直接转移给收藏家。 当脚本运行时，没有人确切知道会产生什么：收藏家不知道，平台不知道，艺术家也不知道。 这对每个人来说都是一个惊喜。

我在 fx(hash) 打开后不久就发布或删除了我的第一个长篇项目。 第一个是 SEA：一个非常简单的项目，在几天内完成，我从中学到了很多东西。 150 个动画版本，快速构建只是为了玩 fx(hash)。

这些作品很快就找到了收藏家。 我和他们中的一些人交谈过，只遇到了可爱的人，我很高兴看到每个人都在这些平台上做什么，成为所有这些发酵和创造力的旁观者，并且通常对算法艺术和 NFT 了如指掌。

这就是我如何在几个月内在该平台上发布了大约 15 个项目的原因。 每次我尝试新技术，质疑美学，测试新概念。

让我告诉你两个我特别喜欢的项目。

桥

BRIDGE 是一个协作项目，我在 GitHub 上发布了代码，并邀请了任何想要贡献的艺术家。 这是一个包含 520 个版本的长篇项目。 这个概念很简单：编写一段代码，在 p5.js 中绘制一座桥，尊重桥面板的给定位置。 每件铸造的作品都有一个默认样式，但收藏家可以在其桥上循环浏览所有 26 种样式。

这个项目让我认识了几位至今仍在交谈的艺术家。 看到相同的约束下产生的风格多样性是令人着迷的。

动脉

我还想提一下 ARTERIA，可能是迄今为止我最引以为豪的 fx(hash) 项目。 它有333个版本。 那时我想花更多的时间，尝试更复杂、更深思熟虑的项目。 有一个制作过程详细描述了它是如何工作的以及它是如何产生的。

ARTERIA 这个名字在古奥克西唐语中的意思是“动脉”。 该项目是对自主代理的探索：遵循一组简单规则的实体，在这里是为了绘制路径。

在 ARTERIA 中，智能体有一个默认行为：它们直线前进，繁殖，并在遇到另一个智能体的轨迹时死亡。 当他们移动时，他们会画小圆圈。 该系统从数十个随机初始参数开始：递归级别、代理的位置和大小、颜色、出生角度、分布。 可能性是无限的。

然后可以在上面应用本地规则。 例如，上半部分的所有特工可能会慢慢转动。 最终结果是初始参数、智能体之间的交互和局部规则的乘积。 这是一件关于简单规则和自主交互中可以出现的美丽和复杂性的作品。

“我本来想成为一名艺术家”

ARTERIA 掉落在 fx(hash) 上取得了成功。 我开始拥有密切关注我的作品、购买和分享我的项目、为我提供建议和支持的收藏家。 这让我更加想要花时间，继续致力于美学，构建更丰富、更复杂的生成器。 情况越来越严重了。

这是 2022 年 6 月录制的播客，其中我接受了巴黎 FauveParis 拍卖行首席执行官 Lucie-Eleonore Riveron 的采访。 我谈论了我是如何来到这里的，也谈论了让我很难将自己视为艺术家的冒名顶替综合症，谈论了我对“真正的艺术家”的先入之见，以及我下一步想要做什么。

我已经详细讨论过 fx(hash) 是一个开放平台：任何人都可以随时发布项目，并且有很多优秀的工作。 但还有很多其他的。 有些同样开放；有些则同样开放。其他人则要求项目由策展小组选择。 像 gm.studio 或 Art Blocks 及其策展部分这样的平台可能要求极高。

因此，我给自己设定了一个挑战：我是否也可以尝试一下我一直在远处欣赏的平台之一？

他妈的

我一直在尝试一个新的长篇项目 FOLRADURA，发表在 256ART 上。 它通过数学、物理、噪音和机会的结合来探索有机图案的创造。

FOLRADURA 基于一个主要概念：局部修饰符。 修改器将局部效果（例如吸引力）应用于数十万个点的网格。 您看到的是这些点在其初始位置和最终位置之间的路径。 每个版本都使用一种或两种类型的修饰符。 它们可以以不同的方式放置，有时是随机的，有时是在网格上。 每一种都会根据其配置和类型产生非常不同的效果：正方形、螺旋形、线条、波浪。

每个点都受到每个修饰符的影响。 所有这些复杂性产生了非常有机的外观和大量的细节。 该项目取得了成功，它展示了简单规则和自主交互所带来的美感和复杂性。 如果你想要更多，还有一个制作。

简介

由于喜欢在 ARTERIA 上与自主代理合作，我决定重新采用这个概念并将其推向新的方向。

INTRICADA 这个名称在古奥克西唐语中的意思是“交错”。 该项目探索了涌现与控制之间的平衡，这是算法艺术中反复出现的主题。

INTRICADA 建立在与 ARTERIA 类似的自主代理之上。 代理绘制非常小的点并遵循简单的规则。 我将 INTRICADA 设计为模拟：设置初始条件，然后观察结果。 每一件作品都是数以千计的不可预见后果的结果。

INTRICADA 的独特之处在于可能的结果多种多样。 许多参数会影响代理的初始位置和方向、调色板等等。 每一种组合都会产生真正独特的结果。

INTRICADA 提供多种尺度的视觉体验。 从远处看，一件作品看起来就像相交的圆圈、几何图案、五彩纸屑。 靠近一点，您会发现这些形状是由大量代理轨迹组成的。 再靠近一点，您会发现这些轨迹是由点组成的，每个输出有数十万个点。

INTRICADA 作为开放版本被放弃，这意味着可以创建的作品数量没有限制，只有时间限制。 我很荣幸被 Bright Moments 选为 2023 年 3 月的本月艺术家。 《光明时刻》的特别之处在于他们非常注重为他们发布的项目赋予物理和人文维度。 INTRICADA 在世界各地的城市展出：纽约、伦敦、墨西哥城、威尼斯海滩、柏林和东京。 一次难以置信的经历。

来源

自 2022 年 7 月以来，我一直在与 INTRICADA 一起与我的老朋友兼业务合作伙伴 Matthieu Segret 进行合作。 从我来到这个世界的最初几天起，我就一直告诉他我的发现。 没过多久他就被诱惑了，他的 fx(hash) 个人资料值得一看。

到 2022 年夏天，算法艺术已经占据了我们一年的大部分空闲时间，我们不断地谈论它。 一个想法慢慢成形：如果我们将我们的技能集中到艺术合作中会怎样？ 找到一个想法，享受我们自己，尽力而为，看看结果如何。

对于这个项目，Matthieu 希望尝试使用纹理并尝试在渲染中实现物理质量；我想研究数学概念。

这是几个月的思考、集思广益、试验、编码、调试、怀疑和喜悦的开始。 几个月后，我们找到了我们的主线：用来自世界各地的彩色倒影以各种形式抽象地代表水。 在那段时期，我们经常租用一些地方一起工作，有时是在海边或河边，以寻找灵感。

我们已经详细讲述了该项目是如何组合在一起的，所以让我先跳到几个月。

到 2023 年初，我们对所拥有的一切感到非常满意。 这几乎肯定是我们做过的最好的项目。 作为两个人，花那么多时间在这件事上，让我们处理每一个细节。 我们有一个项目、一个名称和一个演示文稿。 现在我们必须找到一个地方来发布它。 我们将其推广到多个平台，包括我一直梦想的平台。

五月初传来消息：gm.studio想要发布它。 gm.studio 的特别之处在于策展小组不知道艺术家的名字。 仅基于项目，它就可以提供更公平、更具包容性的选择。 我们喜欢这个平台，也喜欢他们的选择。 最重要的是，这是第一次由评审团一致选择一个项目。 我们非常高兴，毫不犹豫地签了字。

《The Source》于 2023 年 7 月 31 日在 gm.studio 上发布。 我会让你欣赏他们为这个场合制作的预告片。

巴黎光明时刻的目的地

冒险并没有就此停止。 马蒂厄和我决定继续合作。 从 The Source 的源代码开始，我们构建了一个基于同一个宇宙的全新项目：The Destination。

《目的地》是一首对好奇心的颂歌，讲述了人们可以采取的路径的多样性以及有待发现的众多主题。 每颗行星或恒星都代表一个值得探索的领域。 马蒂厄和我结合了我们自己的热情，将这个系列变成了现实。它庆祝实现目标的整个旅程。 这个标题也是对我们第一次合作的致敬。

这个项目把我们带到了巴黎的光明时刻，在那里我们见到了我们的收藏家，以及我们欣赏并定期交谈的艺术家。

《光明时刻》大结局，威尼斯

随后，Bright Moments 邀请我再次与他们合作举办他们的最后一场活动，这次是在 2024 年威尼斯双年展期间展示的一个独特项目。 这件作品的独特之处在于它结合了六十多位对画廊历史至关重要的艺术家的作品。

很高兴看到我的作品在如此非凡的环境中展出。

弹力

Résilience 是一个非常个人化的算法项目，诞生于一年来对视觉模式和纹理的探索。 它于 2024 年 11 月在 gm.scribe 上发布。 每个版本都代表着生命中的一个时刻，一次被克服的考验，一次缓慢但真实的转变。 这部作品取材于对我的生活产生重大影响的健康经历——听觉过敏和耳鸣，它是关于人类适应、治愈和前进的能力。

通过抽象的形式、不断变化的调色板和微妙的动画，Résilience 邀请收藏家在特定的作品中找到与他们自己的道路的共鸣。 这是一部关于坚持、关于重建、关于希望的作品。

这也是我第一个关于比特币的项目。

接下来会发生什么

我有一些正在进行中的项目、正在展示和正在制作中的项目。 我还希望有机会在我自己的城市蒙彼利埃，或者至少在法国，更广泛地展示我的作品和算法艺术。

我很高兴向人们介绍这个世界。 我在 2023 年图卢兹 DevFest 上以及最近在 MiXiT 和 MontpellierJS 上通过自己的方式展示了算法艺术。

如果您想关注，可以在 Twitter 和 Instagram 上关注。 还有 GENART 播客。
